Confidential Computing on NVIDIA HGX™ B300 & HGX™ B200

# Confidential Computing on NVIDIA HGX™ B300 & HGX™ B200 

 Oct 14, 2026 | Yahya Khafif & Mukund Birje | 6 min read 

 Sensitive data used in AI workloads needs to be protected the entire time, from the moment it's stored to the moment it's computed on. That's where the AI infrastructure you use can fall short.

...

Protecting that data has traditionally come down to policy, access controls, audit logs, and contract language. Verda offers confidential computing on NVIDIA GPUs, which replaces that with proof. The hardware protects the workload while it's running, not just before or after, and attestation provides signed proof that its components, like the GPU firmware, match an approved state. This encrypted workload runs on GDPR-compliant infrastructure, which matters when your requirements are tied to where data is processed, not just how it's protected. 

 With confidential computing, sensitive data that used to have to stay on-prem to meet compliance requirements can now be used for inference and fine tuning on infrastructure the company doesn't own. The same holds for organizations licensing a model or serving it to customers on infrastructure they don't control: the weights stay as protected as they would on hardware the company owns outright. And for anyone building a product where privacy is the pitch, it is the difference between a claim in a privacy policy and a claim backed by cryptographic proof. 

 Confidential computing on Verda runs on three NVIDIA GPUs, each with different configuration support: 

| GPU | Available configuration |
| --- | --- |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO™ 6000 Blackwell Server Edition | 1× Blackwell GPU |
| NVIDIA HGX™ B200 | 8× Blackwell GPUs |
| NVIDIA HGX™ B300 | 8× Blackwell Ultra GPUs |

...

Confidential computing on Verda ran at up to 99% of full speed on some configurations, with a cost to throughput and latency minimal enough that most workloads won’t notice the difference.

...

### Setup stack 

| Component | Version / Detail |
| --- | --- |
| GPU | 8× NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs |
| CPU / CC tech | AMD SEV-SNP |
| Driver | 595.58.03 |
| Stack | SGLang v0.5.12-cu130 + PR #28251 + FlashInfer PR #3638, patched onto the same base image both sides |
| Model | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP=8 |
| Client | sglang.bench_serving, ShareGPT-seeded random dataset, seed 42 |

## Getting started 

 Confidential computing on Verda is available today, for regulated inference, fine tuning on sensitive data, and privacy-first AI products. Sign up to deploy and read the docs for setup and verification steps. Get in touch with us for custom configurations. 

### DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is now on Verda Inference 

 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is live on Verda Inference: 1M-token context and switchable thinking via an OpenAI-compatible API, from $0.15 per million input tokens.

results.title: How Epsilon Health accelerates radiology AI training with Verda
highlights:
Oct 15, 2026 | Mukund Birje | 4 min read

...

Dedicated capacity. Epsilon Health needed a dedicated NVIDIA HGX™ B300 GPU cluster to scale its compute for the next generation of its models. There was no availability, it was hard to find long-term contracts at reasonable prices, and shared platforms had no capacity either.

...

Epsilon Health partnered with Verda to implement a dedicated instant cluster on Verda’s platform, with NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra (B300) GPUs, chosen specifically for what the hardware generation unlocks, not just for raw compute. 

 Managed infrastructure, hands-off cluster ops. Managed Kubernetes and direct support from Verda's engineering team, including custom scheduling, automated hardware health checks, and help designing a dataset-caching approach, let Epsilon's team focus on model training rather than infrastructure management. 

 High-HBM capacity for native-resolution training. NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra's memory capacity lets Epsilon Health train on X-ray, CT, and MRI data at native resolution instead of downscaling, supporting the large context windows volumetric imaging requires and improving fine-grained detection of faint findings. 

 Blackwell-tuned kernels for training speed. Flash Attention 4 and other libraries built specifically for NVIDIA Blackwell hardware gave Epsilon Health meaningful speedups over an equivalent number of NVIDIA Hopper architecture nodes. 

 Multi-node training at scale. Training runs span multiple nodes at a time, using NVLink and InfiniBand for fast parameter sharding and weight updates across the cluster. 

 Fast availability, on workable terms. Verda provided capacity quickly, at a reasonable price and term length, at a point when dedicated NVIDIA HGX B300 capacity was difficult to find anywhere on the market.

...

Less infrastructure work, more experiments. Managed cluster operations and Kubernetes scheduling freed up engineering time Epsilon's team previously spent on infrastructure, letting them run roughly 5x more experiments per week.

results.title: How ExpressAI protects user privacy with Verda’s Confidential Computing
highlights:
Oct 22, 2026 | Mukund Birje | 4 min read

...

Making sure ExpressAI worked the same way is what led them to Verda's Confidential Computing, running on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.

...

## Solution 

 ExpressVPN partnered with Verda to run ExpressAI inside Confidential Computing on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. 

 Why the newest GPU architecture mattered. ExpressAI couldn't afford to trade privacy for performance. Older or queued hardware would have meant compromising on model quality or speed to get the isolation guarantee, and that tradeoff wasn't acceptable. Getting there also meant ExpressVPN needed more than rack space from a partner. Because ExpressVPN operates its own enclaves and attestation pipeline rather than adopting a pre-built version, it needed a partner willing to work at that level of detail, down to network and firewall configuration for the enclave environment itself, rather than handing over a fixed, closed system. 

 What they built together. That co-engineering went further than infrastructure setup. Most confidential computing implementations at the time were limited to a single GPU. Together, ExpressVPN and Verda enabled confidential computing across multi-node configurations on NVIDIA HGX™ B200, including early support for distributed secure GPU clusters and validation of performance and isolation at production scale.

...

- A claim backed by proof, not policy. ExpressVPN can point to something concrete instead of a policy promise: a specific enclave, with its own measurement, that a user can check for their own session. Every logged-in user has access to their own Attestation Report, showing that proof. 
- Independently audited, not self-certified. ExpressAI's architecture has been reviewed by Cure53, so the privacy guarantee is checked by a third party rather than resting on ExpressVPN's own word. 
- Multi-node confidential computing in production. ExpressAI runs on multi-node NVIDIA HGX™ B200 confidential computing, built jointly with Verda, and validated for large-scale inference. That's a step past single-GPU confidential computing, which is where most public confidential computing offerings still sit today.
